newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU raids firms in price fixing probe.
newsitem.headline: EU raids firms in price fixing probe.

text.p: Authorities raided the European headquarters of agribusiness giant Archer Daniels Midland Co. and other non-European Union companies in a price fixing investigation involving amino acids used in animal feed, the European Commission said Thursday.
The dawn raids were staged Wednesday at the companies' headquarters in Germany and Britain and were continuing Thursday, a European Union spokesman said in confirming the investigation.

"I can confirm our inspectors have been conducting (raids) at the European headquarters of a series of companies. ... Our inspectors are still around, apparently in Germany and the United Kingdom," an EU spokesman said.
He confirmed that Decatur, Ill.-based Archer Daniel Midlands (ADM) was being investigated, as the company said Wednesday but declined to name the other companies involved.
Another EU source said later that three companies were being investigated, including ADM, and that they were all based outside the 15-nation European Union but had operations in Europe.

ADM, which pleaded guilty to price-fixing charges in the United States last year, said Wednesday it and several of its European subsidiaries were among the targets of an anti-competitive practices probe by the commission.

ADM said in a statement the commission was probing the possible participation of major manufacturers in anti-competitive practices or agreements in certain EU markets for amino acids, including the feed additive lysine.

EU sources confirmed lysine was one and probably the main product concerned. They said the European market for the product, used in pigs and poultry, was worth an annual 250 million European currency units ($282 million).
They said that competitors had complained about alleged price fixing, but declined to give names. They added that some companies were cooperating with the EU's competition officials.
ADM pleaded guilty in the United States last year to fixing prices of lysine and the food additive citric acid, and paid a record $100 million in fines.
The U.S. Justice Department probe also resulted in charges against Ajinimoto Co. Inc. and Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co. Ltd. of Japan and Sewon America Inc.
ADM said the commission probe was in its early stages and the outcome could not be predicted.
The commission can fine firms found guilty of colluding on market share or price rigging up to 10 percent of their annual revenue, depending on the offences and how long they last.
ADM stock was down 25 cents at $20.75 in consolidated late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
